market_narrative.headline: Fed/rates keeps risk appetite constructive but selective as investors await confirmation
market_narrative.summary: US equities are carrying a constructive but selective bias as Fed/rates, oil/energy, inflation shape positioning. Investors are balancing selective leadership against the risk that policy, rates or growth data broadens the pressure.

key_forces.text: Headline and policy uncertainty keep the risk premium elevated

key_forces.label: Main theme
key_forces.text: Positioning is waiting for confirmation from futures, Treasury yields and opening breadth

watch_next: futures, Treasury yields and opening breadth

index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (253), oil/energy (145), inflation (133), growth/jobs (68). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 339 positive, 196 negative, and 1330 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.

themes.title: Fed Policy & Rate Path
themes.current_view: Fed policy is still restrictive, but investors are watching whether softer data pulls rate-cut expectations forward.
themes.what_changed: The rate path is becoming the main valuation channel for long-duration equity exposure.
themes.why_it_matters: Rate cuts support multiples, but cuts driven by weaker growth can also pressure earnings expectations.

market_impact.equities: Neutral for indexes, supportive for duration if growth holds.
sectors: Negative: Banks if yield curves flatten

themes.current_view: Growth risk is the key constraint on equity upside.
themes.what_changed: Investors need to separate healthy cooling from recession risk.
themes.why_it_matters: Labor and demand data affect both forward earnings and the policy reaction function.

themes.current_view: AI leadership remains the strongest equity-specific macro channel.
themes.what_changed: Mega-cap technology and semiconductor narratives continue to carry index leadership.
themes.why_it_matters: Concentrated leadership can support indexes while also raising valuation and crowding risk.
